subject: pixelDungeonProps
pitch:
Category: Prop group.
Subject: dungeon props: chest, torches, barrels, bones, spike trap.
Style: pixel art.
reasoning:
I'm planning a pixel-art prop set in TypeScript, sketching out a stone floor slab, a wooden chest with iron bands, wall torches, and stacked barrels to keep the module efficient yet visually rich.

Since there's no creature, I just need one root joint, with a child hinge joint for the chest lid. I'll import the pixel kit utilities and work out the spatial layout -- base slab dimensions, chest and barrel placement, torch posts, and scattering bones and a spike trap across the floor relative to a shared ground height.

Now I'm planning the pixel textures: dithered gray stone bricks, horizontal wood plank rows for the chest, and vertical stave stripes for barrels with separate iron hoop cylinders. I'm thinking through using a lathe geometry with a bulging profile for the barrel shape, painted with wood tones via cell-based coloring.

I'm also sketching a bone texture using simple cell paint, and planning torches with crossed billboard planes carrying a flame texture, wrapped in a glow effect for emissive light.

For the physical torch, I'm thinking a wooden post with an iron bracket cup, dark cloth wrapping, and flame on top, plus a stone base for floor-standing versions. For the chest, I'm building the body as a tiled wood box and designing a stepped, blocky lid split into two boxes to suggest a pitched top, posed slightly open at the back hinge.

Negative rotation on the hinge axis lifts the front of the lid to show it ajar, and I want a glowing pile of gold coin boxes mounded on top of the body so it peeks out when the lid opens. I'm also adding iron band boxes wrapped slightly wider than the body for detail.

I'm setting up a helper function to create box parts with colors or textures attached to bones, and sketching out a lathe profile for barrel shapes with a tapered base and rim.

Now I'm defining the actual barrel dimensions, working out the outline points for the lathe geometry and figuring out where to place cylindrical hoops along the barrel's height by interpolating the radius at different y-positions.

Skipping the lying-barrel idea since it adds complexity, I'll keep three standing barrels instead, maybe stacking one on top of two for variety. For bones, I'm planning a helper that builds a long bone as a rod with knob-shaped ends in bone color.

For the skull, I'm designing it as a cranium box plus a separate jaw box, with eye sockets, nose, and teeth added as small inset boxes for a pixel-art look, slightly protruding from the front face. The ribcage will build off a spine structure.

Writing rib curve paths...

Now for the spike trap: a darker stone slab with a 3x3 grid of holes for iron spikes, using cone sweeps with varying heights and a blood gradient on the tips, plus boxes to frame the border.

I'm adding dark holes under each spike and a glowing red rune in the corner of the pressure plate, then thinking about extra details like scattered coins. For lighting, I'm designing floor torch stands with a stone base, wood post, iron collar, cloth head, and a flame made from pixel-art textures with an orange glow core.

Still writing flame pixel art...

Now I'm setting up the card mesh config with flow direction and cross-facing, confirming the glow effect applies correctly with the pixelated texture, and moving on to defining the stone tile brick pattern.

For the brick texture, I'm writing a deterministic hash function to shade each brick, alternating row offsets for a staggered pattern, and marking mortar lines with a dark color while giving the top edge of each brick a lighter highlight for depth.

Writing hash function...

Now I'm thinking through how to apply this stone texture to the floor geometry -- a single large slab stretches the tile texels too much at that scale, so instead I should build the floor from a grid of smaller flagstone tiles (6x4, each 0.4 units square) where the texel size lines up cleanly to a 32x32 texture resolution.

I'm sketching two distinct textures: FLAG with a beveled edge and cracks for the floor tiles, and BRICK with a border for other surfaces. Writing texture generation code...

Now I'm sizing the chest body using tileBox with wood texture, adjusting texel size so the plank pattern fits the box dimensions proportionally. I'm also setting up the color palette constants for iron, gold, bone, and red accents used across the chest hardware.

Writing wood/bone paint logic...

Now I'm setting up the chest's joint structure: a root joint and a lid joint with a hinge rotation to pose it open, plus positioning the chest and adding iron band details around it.

Still placing dimensions for the lid pieces, lock, and hasp...

I'm scattering a few small gold coin boxes near the chest with a subtle glow, plus adding a rotated gem on the mound using a tilted box shape. Now I'm positioning the barrels nearby, working out their radius and spacing so one can rest on top of the other two in front of the chest.

I'm also placing a couple of torches flanking the scene, checking their coordinates so they sit just outside the barrel stack without clipping into the base boundary.

Then I'm positioning the spike trap and chest so their footprints don't overlap, nudging the trap's center and size until both fit cleanly within the available space.

Finally I'm scattering bones near the front-left corner—a skull, crossing femurs, and a ribcage—spreading them out for a natural debris look.

Writing femur placement coordinates...

Skipping yaw rotation for simplicity, keeping the face oriented toward the viewer. I'm adding eye socket boxes, a nose shape, and small teeth boxes along the jaw's front edge to give the skull some facial detail.

For the helper function, I need to be careful that parts default to attaching to the root bone explicitly, rather than accidentally binding to whichever joint is nearest—otherwise facial details near the lid joint could attach incorrectly. I'll skip adding ember or light-pool effects on the floor for now.

For gold materials I'm applying a glow effect at moderate intensity, which works fine even with flat hex colors. Then I'm detailing the spike trap: building a brick frame around a dark inset plate, cutting a grid of holes, and placing spikes at randomized heights using a seeded rng for variation.

Each spike is oriented upward with a thin radius, using four-sided geometry for a crisp look, and I'm giving them a gradient paint that blends iron and blood tones along their vertical axis.

I'm varying the spike heights so the center ones stand taller than the surrounding ones, and adding small glowing red rune-like boxes at the frame corners for a warning effect, then starting a torch function that builds a stone base tile and post.

Continuing the torch design, I'm layering a wooden post, iron collar, and cloth-wrapped head, then adding flame card sprites with a glowing orange ember core at the top, aiming for a total torch height of roughly 1.1 units.

For the sink, I'm planning a floor made of a 6x4 grid of tile planes spaced across a 2.4x1.6 area, with thin dark gaps between them backed by a dark underlay box so nothing shows through. I'm also considering generating two slightly different tile texture variants from different seeds so the floor doesn't look too uniform.

Writing tile pixel textures...

Adding gold coins near the chest, scattering rubble pieces with randomized stone colors along the edges without overlapping other props, and building a barrel using a lathe function with configurable position and scale.

Still writing helper functions...
